untagged_candidates.title: Lines that seem to name someone but have no person tag yet (candidates to tag)

caveats: MPAP_4: only 10 of 47 included pages are tagged (593 pages in the manuscript), so people and occupations are partial.

answer.headline: Partly, yes: Conti already holds 75 unapproved person tags, but on finished pages they cover only RS1128 and RS1138; a rough pattern search finds 326 more candidate lines.
answer.answer:
Yes, but nothing has been checked yet. Among the finished MPAP 4 pages, person tags exist on only two pages: RS1128 (39 lines) and RS1138 (22 lines), 61 lines in all [tagged_pages]. Those lines carry 75 person tags. All of them are Claude suggestions: the coverage shows 0 of 459 tags approved across the manuscript. The most frequent names are Francesca di Tommaso di Francesco Davizi (4 tags), then Bindo di messer Iacopo de' Bardi, Ruberto di Bindo de' Bardi and Tommaso di Francesco Davizi (3 each). Deo di Vanni, Doffo di Giovanni de' Bardi and Cola di Guglielmo appear twice each [people]. Several tags are a first name only (Giovanna, Maddalena, Selvaggia, Antonio, Dea, Dada), so they cannot yet be told apart or linked across pages.

The tags also record each person's part in the entry. Of the 75 tags, 39 are debtors and 16 are only mentioned. There are 10 beneficiaries, 5 heirs, 2 officers, 2 testators and 1 creditor [roles]. Most debtors come from RS1128, a list of debitori. The beneficiaries, heirs and testators come from RS1138, a will.

To show how much is still untagged, Conti searched the untagged lines of finished pages with a simple name pattern. It matched titles such as monna, ser, messer, prete and frate, and the shape 'Name di/de/del Name'. That found 326 lines on 22 pages, led by RS1158 (37), RS1144 (24), RS1153 (22), RS1140, RS1152 and RS1195 (19 each), RS1129 and RS1139 (18 each) [untagged_candidates]. The search is crude in both directions. It matches lines that name no person, such as 'di xxvii dagosto an̄o mccclxxxiii', 'E al le mura del comune di firenze' and 'la cōpagnia di sandonato'. And because it looks for expanded words, it misses the diplomatic abbreviations the pages actually use: mō for monna, ß for ser, mesß for messer. So 326 is a rough measure of the work left, not a count of persons.

In practice, the 'program' that fits best is Conti's existing Claude tagging pass. It reads each line and proposes person tags with a role, and you approve or reject them in Conti. It has been run on a pilot of 10 pages, and of the finished pages only RS1128 and RS1138 have person tags. Running it on the 22 pages listed above would give suggestions for the rest of the finished set, still to be reviewed before any count or network is relied on.

caveats: All 75 person tags are unreviewed Claude suggestions (0 approved), so names, spellings and roles may be wrong.

Name counts are tag counts, not counts of distinct people. One line can carry two tags (e.g. RS1128 line 6, Filippo di brunetto … ⁊ macho), and first-name-only tags (Giovanna, Maddalena, Antonio) may be several different people or one person also tagged under a full name.

The 326 candidate lines come from a regular expression written in expanded spelling. It misses diplomatic abbreviations (mō, ß, mesß) and catches non-persons (dates, the comune, a compagnia), so it is neither complete nor precise.
The 'people' list in results.json shows only the top 30 names; the full list of 75 tags is in Conti.
